171:
(a) In order to be eligible for a consumption on the premises license, a hotel must:
(1) Be used and held out to the public as a place where food is served and consumed and sleeping accommodations are offered to guests for adequate pay;
(2) Contain 50 or more rooms used for the sleeping accommodations of guests; and
(3) Contain one or more public dining rooms, with adequate and sanitary full-service kitchen facilities.
(b) A hotel may consist of a single building or may consist of two or more buildings located on the same premises and used in connection with the hotel operation.
(c) A facility which is styled as a motel, motor lodge, inn, or other similar appellation may be licensed as a hotel if it meets the requirements of this section.
(d) A hotel may grant permission for the operation of a lounge, restaurant, or supper club on its premises; such an operation may be granted a consumption on the premises license if it meets the other applicable requirements of this chapter.
(e) Notwithstanding any other provisions of this chapter to the contrary, any hotel (as the term "hotel" is commonly used and without regard to the requirements of this section), inn, or other establishment which offers overnight accommodations to the public for hire, may provide in-room service of alcoholic beverages if such establishment:
(1) Holds a valid city package license or a valid city consumption on the premises license or both; and
(2) Has been authorized to provide in-room service by the state revenue commissioner.
(f) For purposes of this section, the term "in-room service" consists of:
(1) The delivery of alcoholic beverages in unbroken packages by an employee of the hotel to a registered guest's room when such alcoholic beverages have been ordered by the guest and when the guest shall be billed for the cost of such alcoholic beverages at the time of delivery and when the sale of such alcoholic beverages is completed at the time of delivery; and
(2) The provision of a cabinet or other facility located in a hotel's guestroom which contains alcoholic beverages and which is provided upon request of the guest and which is accessible by lock and key only to the guest and for which the sale of alcoholic beverages contained therein is final at the time requested except for a credit which may be given to the guest for any unused portion.
(g) Except as otherwise provided in this section, in-room service of alcoholic beverages shall be subject to all restrictions and limitations in this chapter relative to the sale of alcoholic beverages. In-room service sales delivered by room service shall be authorized only on such days and only during such hours as the sale of alcoholic beverages is otherwise authorized.
(h) All alcoholic beverages sold pursuant to this section shall be purchased from a licensed wholesale dealer and shall be subject to all taxes imposed under this chapter, including the excise tax on the retail sale by the drink of alcoholic beverages containing distilled spirits.
(Ord. No. 2017-06, § 1(Exh. A), 3-7-2017)

(a) In order to be eligible for a consumption on the premises license, a private club must be a nonprofit association which is organized under the laws of the state and which:
(1) Has been in existence at least one year prior to the filing of its application for a license;
(2) Has at least 75 regular dues-paying members:
(3) Is organized and operated exclusively for pleasure, recreation, and other nonprofit purposes;
(4) Owns, hires, or leases a building or space within a building for the reasonable use of its members, which building or space:
a. Has suitable kitchen and dining room space and equipment;
b. Is staffed with a sufficient number of employees for cooking, preparing, and serving meals for its members and guests; and
c. Has no member, officer, agent, or employee directly or indirectly receiving in the form of salary or other compensation any profits from the sale of alcoholic beverages beyond a fixed salary.

(c) No alcoholic beverage license shall be granted to a private club organized or operated primarily for the selling or serving of alcoholic beverages.

203:
(a) An employee pouring permit shall be required for:
(1) Any employee of a consumption on the premises licensee who dispenses, sells, serves, takes orders for, and/or mixes alcoholic beverages, or serves in any managerial position; and
(2) Any employee of an alcoholic beverage caterer who is engaged in handling, selling, or serving alcoholic beverages; provided, however, employees whose duties are limited solely to those of busboy or cook or dishwasher shall be excluded.
(b) An employee pouring permit shall not be required for:
(1) The licensee to whom an alcoholic beverage license has been issued under this chapter.
(2) Any person authorized by law to serve alcoholic beverage and is working at a temporary, nonprofit fundraising event for which a temporary alcohol permit to sell alcoholic beverages has been issued under this chapter.
(c) No licensee shall employ any person required to have a pouring permit until such person has procured such permit.
(d) Any person required to obtain a pouring permit shall apply to the police department for such permit on forms prescribed by the chief of police or his designee.
(e) When a person applies for an alcohol server's permit, the chief of police, or his designee, shall have a complete and extensive search made to determine if there is a police record of such person. If the search reveals a conviction for an alcohol related offense within five (5) years of the date of the application, or conviction of any felony within five years of the date of the application or evidence that the person's employment would adversely affect the public health, safety, or welfare, issuance of a permit shall be denied. A plea of nolo contendere shall be considered a conviction. If at the time of application the applicant is charged with any of the offenses prescribed in this subsection, consideration of the application shall be dismissed without prejudice and the applicant shall be allowed to reapply upon final disposition of any such charge.
(f) When any pouring permit is denied, the chief of police shall issue to the applicant or permit holder a letter within 30 days stating that the person does not meet the requirements of this chapter, describing the requirements not deemed satisfied, and that upon request the chief of police will refer the matter and any evidence the person cares to submit on his/her behalf to the city manager for consideration and, that, if requested, a meeting may be scheduled with the city manager at which time the person shall be provided an opportunity to explain why the permit should not be denied. A request for consideration and any documentation the person wishes to have considered by the city manager upon his/her review must be received by the chief of police within ten days of the date of the denial letter. If the person requests consideration by the city manager as permitted by this paragraph, the person shall present any request for a meeting with the city manager in the request for consideration. The city manager shall consider all information provided to him/her by the chief of police and the applicant/permit holder and issue his/her decision within ten days of submission of the record to him by the chief of police. A meeting with the city manager allowed by this provision shall also be scheduled and held within the ten-day period following submission of the record by the chief of police. If the city manager affirms denial of the permit, written notice shall be provided to the applicant/permit holder by certified mail at the address provided by the applicant/permit holder, describing the reason(s) for denial of the permit. If dissatisfied with the decision, the applicant/permit holder may file a written notice of appeal with the city clerk within five days of receipt of the decision at which point the matter shall be placed on the agenda of the next meeting of the governing authority occurring no earlier than ten days from the filing of the notice of appeal. The decision of the governing authority shall be final unless, to the extent the decision of the governing authority is appealable or otherwise subject to review, such appeal or review is sought in the Superior Court of Paulding County by filing a petition for a writ of certiorari in compliance with O.C.G.A. § 5-4-1 et seq.
(g) Only one server's permit per individual will be issued for employment at any and all establishments within the city. The permit will be valid for a period of one year and shall be renewed on or before its expiration. Persons applying for the permit shall make themselves available for photographing, fingerprinting, and such other investigation as may be required by the city police department. The application for a pouring permit shall be accompanied by the requisite fee in an amount as set in section 6-88.
(h) A new search may be conducted on any person issued an employee pouring permit if the chief of police receives information which warrants such a new search.
(i) If the new search reveals evidence that the person no longer meets the requirements of this chapter, the permit may be suspended or revoked as provided in subsection 6-87(a)(3) of this chapter.
(j) It shall be unlawful for a person whose pouring permit has been revoked and upon whom demand for return of the card has been made to refuse to return the card or to alter, conceal, deface, or destroy the card.
(Ord. No. 2017-06, § 1(Exh. A), 3-7-2017)
204:
Any licensee who has any disciplinary action taken against him or any of his employees who sell, take orders for, deliver, or handle alcoholic beverages by any governmental authority (municipal, county, state, or federal) shall notify the chief of police and the city clerk of such action within five days of such action. 208:
(a) Imposed. There is imposed upon the retail sale of drinks containing distilled spirits in the city a tax in the amount of three percent of the purchase price of the drink to the consumer. A record of each sale shall be made in writing and maintained for inspection by any authorized agent of the city.
(b) Licensee to collect and remit. Every consumption on the premises licensee shall collect the tax imposed by this section from purchasers of drinks containing distilled spirits. (a) If the city has cause to believe that a return or the amount of tax paid to the city by a licensee is not proper, the city may compute and determine the amount due on the basis of any information available. One or more deficiency determinations may be made of the amount due for any month.

213:

216:
This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the City of Hiram, Georgia "Special Events Ordinance."
(Ord. No. 2014-02, § l(Exh. A), 5-6-2014; Ord. No. 2024-09, § 1 (Exh. A), 7-2-2024)
218:
Except where otherwise permitted by this chapter, it is unlawful for any person, group of persons, organization, association, club, or other entity to conduct or cause to be conducted any special event in the city without having first obtained a valid special event permit from the city. Permitting, as described in the following sections, is separate and distinct from the process in which one must appear before the governing authority to obtain permission to host a special event on city-owned property. The permit issued must be displayed prominently by the producer during and throughout the special event at the location of the special event or be available upon request for review and inspection. Special event permits are temporary and shall not vest any permanent property rights. Issued permits are effective only for the time period described on the permit. Special events are limited to the hours of operation specified in the permit. In no instance shall a special event be permitted to occur over the course of any more than three consecutive calendar days.
(Ord. No. 2014-02, § l(Exh. A), 5-6-2014; Ord. No. 2024-09, § 1 (Exh. A), 7-2-2024)
219:
Except where otherwise permitted by this chapter, not less than 30 days nor more than 120 days prior to the special event, the producer shall apply for a special event permit and provide the following information and materials:
(1) The name, mailing address, email address, and telephone number of the producer of the special event and, if a corporation, partnership, or other entity, the name, address, email address, and telephone number of a person designated as responsible for compliance with all provisions of this chapter and other applicable chapters, all jointly known as the "producer."
(2) A description of the special event proposed.
(3) The date(s), location(s), and hours of operation proposed for the special event.
(4) A schedule, however tentative, of proposed activities, including a description of each vendor for the sale of food, food products, goods, merchandise, services, or alcohol contemplated for the special event. The city must be provided at the earliest opportunity any update to the schedule and accompanying description as the schedule of activities becomes more definite or changes.
(5) An estimate of the number of participants in the special event and projected attendance for the special event. The producer is required to promptly update the city on any significant changes or anticipated changes in these figures.
(6) A description of any services anticipated as being needed from the city. The producer is required to promptly update this description and notify the city at the earliest opportunity as any need or anticipated need for services changes.
(7) A description of any of the following elements contemplated for use or need in conducting the special event: closing (foil or partial) of a public street; blocking or obstructing public property; the provision of (whether by sale or otherwise) merchandise, food, or beverages on public property or on private property where not otherwise allowed; the erection, use, or installation of a tent, canopy, stage, trailer, grandstand, bleachers, or other structure; pyrotechnics or sound amplification devices; placement and use of portable toilets; and signage. Use of signage is permitted and regulated only in accordance with the city's sign ordinance found in article XII of the City of Hiram Zoning Ordinance.
(8) A plan for responding to medical and other public safety incidents and emergencies occurring during the special event.
(9) A plan for parking along with plans for restroom facilities and the collection and removal of rubbish, garbage, and any other waste byproducts generated by the special event. An acceptable plan must provide for the immediate removal of all rubbish, garbage, and any other waste byproducts generated by the special event upon the conclusion of the special event or, for multi-day events, each day of a multiday event. For multi-day special events, an acceptable plan must provide for removal of all rubbish, garbage, and any other waste byproducts generated each day; provided, however, that exceptions, with written approval from the city manager, may be provided for certain types of rubbish, garbage, and other waste byproducts where daily removal for a multi-day event is not reasonably practicable and the public's health, welfare, and safety would reasonably be determined not to be endangered.
(10) A reasonably accurate depiction of the location of the special event and its boundaries and, further, identifying all buildings, structures, parking, and curb cuts already existing on the property proposed for the special event and immediately adjacent to the property. Also identified on the depiction shall be the locations for any temporary structures, including toilet facilities, and parking to be utilized with the special event.
The 30—120 day window for applying for a special event permit is waived for special events proposed in response to immediate, current events defined as events occurring within seven days prior to the proposed special event. In such instances the producer of the special event is required to submit the application required by this section no later than 72 hours prior to the special event, and, if not practicable, the producer shall give the city manager written notice of the special event at least 24 hours prior to its commencement and provide with the notice as much of the information required in this section as is possible and practicable.
(Ord. No, 2014-02, § l(Exh, A), 5-6-2014; Ord. No. 2024-09, § 1 (Exh. A), 7-2-2024)
220:
In addition to the information required above in an application for a special event permit, the following materials and information must be provided in support of and in addition to the application, all of which must be provided before an application will be considered:
(1) If the producer is a corporation, the state and date of incorporation, a representation that the corporation is qualified to do business in Georgia, and the name and address of the registered agent for service of process for the corporation in Georgia,
(2) A sworn declaration that the producer is in compliance with the State of Georgia SAVE and E-Verify requirements or that the producer is not subject to those requirements, describing the reason(s) for any claimed exemption with sufficient particularity to permit a determination of the bona fides of the claim.
(3) The producer's State of Georgia Department of Revenue sales and/or use tax registration number or an explanation describing the reason(s) for any claimed exemption with sufficient particularity to permit a determination of the bona fides of the claim.
(4) identification of any location(s) within the prior 12 months where the producer conducted a similar special event,
(5) If the special event is to be held on private property, notarized, written permission of the property owner or his/her duly authorized representative.
(6) A legible copy of any current occupation tax certificate issued by a governing body in the State of Georgia. if the producer cannot produce a duly issued occupation tax certificate and is not otherwise exempted from compliance, then the producer must, as a condition for a permit, file for an occupation tax certificate from the city. If an exemption is claimed from payment of an occupation tax, the producer shall describe the exemption with sufficient particularity to determine the bona fides of such a claim.
(7) Copies of written notices informing residences and businesses adjacent to the event area of the intent to host a special event. If the special event involves a parade, procession, or other event without a centralized location, this notification requirement may be waived by the city manager upon request. This notification requirement may also be waived if the city manager determines it would be unreasonable and unduly burdensome in light of the number of residences and businesses to be notified.
(8) Proof of comprehensive liability insurance naming the city as an additional insured. Such insurance must provide at a minimum $1,000,000.00 of coverage for personal injury per person and $1,000,000.00 of property damage coverage covering all claims arising from a permit issued under this chapter. The city manager may waive or reduce this requirement for a special event that:
a. Will not require or involve one or more of the following activities: closing (full or partial) of a public street; blocking or obstructing public property; the provision of merchandise, food, or beverages (whether by sale or otherwise); the erection, use, or installation of a tent, canopy, stage, trailer, grandstand, bleachers, or any other structure; use of any kind of pyrotechnics or sound amplification devices; or placement and use of portable toilets; and
b. Is in response to an immediate, current event defined as national, state, or local event or incident occurring within seven days prior to the proposed special event; or
c. Is produced by an entity or organization recognized by the Federal Internal Revenue Service as satisfying the requirements of 26 U.S.C. § 501(c) or a charitable organization subject to and governed by O.C.G.A. § 43-17-1 et seq. Proper proof of Section 501(c) status and/or registration as required by O.C.G.A. § 43-17-1 et seq. is required.
In exercising this discretion, the city manager shall consider the nature of the activities planned for the participants in the proposed special event; the risk of potential injury or harm to private property and private persons arising from the activities planned for the participants in the proposed special event; and the risk of potential injury or harm to public property arising from the activity planned for the participants in the proposed special event.
(9) The producer shall provide a written agreement in a form satisfactory to the city providing that the producer shall defend, pay, and hold harmless the city, its elected and appointed officials, employees, and agents from liability for all personal and property damages arising from any acts or omissions resulting from a special event, inclusive also of any claims for attorneys' fees and costs connected with such claims, except for such claims arising solely from the negligent acts of the city, its elected and appointed officials, employees, and agents.
(10) Such other information as may be reasonably requested by the city and reasonably related to the scope and scale of the special event, how it is to be conducted, and the other information required by this chapter to be provided.
(11) In addition, the producer shall confer with the appropriate city representatives and establish an acceptable plan for vehicular/pedestrian traffic, crowd and traffic control, and security for the special event proposed.
(Ord. No. 2014-02, § l(Exh. A), 5-6-2014; Ord. No. 2024-09, § 1 (Exh. A), 7-2-2024)
221:
(a) An application fee shall be paid at the time the application is filed for a special event permit to defray the city's administrative expense and costs. The fee shall be set from time to time as determined by the governing authority. The application fee is nonrefundable.
(b) Exempt from payment of the application fee is any special event on behalf of or seeking to benefit wholly (1) an entity or organization recognized by the Federal Internal Revenue Service as satisfying the requirements of 26 U.S.C. § 501(c) or (2) a charitable organization subject to and governed by O.C.G.A. § 43-17-1 et seq. Proper proof of section 501(c) status and/or registration as required by O.C.G.A. § 43-17-1 et seq. is required for this exemption. The exemption for a charitable organization subject to and governed by O.C.G.A. § 43-17-1 et seq. applies only for a special event seeking to raise support for or awareness of a charitable purpose as that phrase is defined in O.C.G.A. § 43-17-2(3), as amended from time to time.
(Ord. No. 2024-09, § 1 (Exh. A), 7-2-2024)
222:
Any special event permit issued by the city is subject to the following conditions and any other conditions determined to be reasonably necessary to protect the city's public safety, health, welfare, and good order;
(1) The permit is limited to the specific geographic area(s) within which the event is to take place. The producer or other person designated as provided in section 7-4 is responsible for providing for security and sanitation services within the boundaries of the event until the area is cleared of all activities and structures related to the event.
(2) Except as needed for clearing the event area(s) of all activities and related structures, no special event shall continue beyond the time approved on the permit.
(3) The special event must comply with the city's noise ordinance and all other ordinances governing the conduct of the special event.
(4) The use of glass containers within the area designated for the special event is prohibited.
(5) Tents, arbors, stages, grandstands, bleachers, and other temporary facilities or structures to be constructed, erected, and used in conjunction with the special event must be approved, if applicable, by the fire marshal and building inspector.
(6) The city shall have the right to require immediate termination or cessation of a special event if a determination is made that the special event or aspects of the special event create or present an imminent threat to the public's safety, health, welfare, and good order. Upon being notified that the special event or an aspect of the special event must cease, it shall be unlawful for the producer and any participants to allow such activity to continue.
(7) To the extent signage for the special event is desired, compliance with the city's sign ordinance is required.
(8) A permit issued under this chapter may not be assigned or transferred.
(9) A special event permit issued under this chapter is separate and distinct from the additional requirement to obtain permission from the governing authority to host a special event on city-owned property.
(Ord. No. 2014-02, § l(Exh. A), 5-6-2014; Ord. No. 2024-09, § 1 (Exh. A), 7-2-2024)
223:
(a) The city manager or his/her designee shall determine within two business days of receipt of an application if the application is complete. If the application is incomplete, the producer shall be notified of the deficiencies. No further action will be taken in connection with the application and request for a permit until all information required by this chapter has been provided.
(b) Upon providing a complete application and all other information required by this chapter, the application shall be circulated within two business days to each government department whose services would be required or would reasonably be affected by the special event proposed. Each such department shall review the application and provide the city manager or his/her designee with an assessment and evaluation of the impact reasonably to be expected by the special event proposed on the factors identified in section 7-9 below. This review and provision of an assessment and evaluation shall be accomplished within seven business days of circulation absent agreement with the producer for additional time. If additional time is necessary due to the absence of one or more persons who would review the request for a permit and the producer does not agree to additional time to permit the person(s) to review the application and materials, the application may be denied for lack of appropriate review.
(c) Upon receiving the departmental assessment(s) and evaluation(s), the city manager may require the producer to provide additional information or response to address any concern(s) or issue(s) raised if such is reasonably necessary to address any of the factors to be evaluated per section 7-9 below,
(Ord. No. 2024-09, § 1 (Exh. A), 7-2-2024)
225:
(a) The sale of food, food products, and/or merchandise, goods, or services by vendors shall be allowed as a component of a special event, provided that each vendor is authorized in writing by the producer to participate in the event and provided further that each vendor shall be subject to all conditions and limitation imposed in writing for the special event by the producer. The written authorizations and the conditions and limitations imposed by the producer shall be submitted promptly to the city in advance of the special event.
(b) The producer shall be responsible for all vendors as a component of the special event and shall be responsible for designating the location and activities of vendors consistent with a special event permit and any applicable conditions.
(c) Authorized vendors of the producer providing food and/or merchandise for sale are not required to obtain or possess a separate vendor's permit to operate during the special event unless the vendor is a provider of alcoholic beverages as a part of the special event. This provision notwithstanding, food vendors authorized by the producer are required to comply with the rules and regulations of the state and the Paulding County health department as to the preparation and service of food.
(d) The dispensing of alcoholic beverages, by sale or otherwise, as a part of the special event shall be allowed provided that each vendor is authorized to participate by the producer and, provided further, that each vendor dispensing alcoholic beverages shall have been duly licensed by the state, city, or other local governing authority to engage in off-premises dispensation and has complied with all provisions of the city's ordinances relating to the sale or dispensation otherwise of alcoholic beverages off premises.
(e) Each authorized vendor shall prominently display a badge or other notification signifying the vendor's status as one authorized to participate in the special event by the producer.
(f) It shall be unlawful for any unauthorized vendor to engage in any business within a distance of 100 yards of the special event from one hour before the scheduled start time for the special event until one hour after the schedule ending time for the special event. This provision does not preclude the transacting of the usual and customary business of a person or entity possessing a valid occupation tax certificate issued by the city for transacting business at a fixed location that happens to be adjacent to or within 100 yards of the property on which the special event is held.
(Ord. No. 2014-02, § l(Exh. A), 5-6-2014; Ord. No. 2024-09, § 1 (Exh. A), 7-2-2024)
226:
The city may co-sponsor a proposed special event upon a request by an applicant for a special event permit or upon acceptance by a producer of an offer for such co-sponsorship. Co-sponsorship may take the form of a monetary contribution in support of the special event, provision of services in-kind at no cost to the producer, or both. Decisions on whether to participate in the proposed special event as a co-sponsor and what will be provided as a cosponsor are entrusted to the discretion of the governing authority for which no appeal shall be permitted. Cosponsorship of a proposed special event is limited only to those events where the producer is an entity whose primary purpose is to promote economic development in the city or Paulding County or an entity that is a non-profit organization that seeks to promote and advance the health, welfare, or safety of the public or a segment of the public within the city or Paulding County and which has its principal place of business located in the city or Paulding County. As a part of the application process an applicant may request that the city co-sponsor the proposed special event. The request must be in writing, describe with particularity the type(s) of co-sponsorship desired, and describe how the special event proposed will enhance or promote economic development in the city or promote and advance the health, welfare, or safety of the public or a segment of the public within the city or Paulding County,
(Ord. No. 2014-02, § l(Exh. A), 5-6-2014; Ord. No. 2024-09, § 1 (Exh. A), 7-2-2024)
227:
Nothing about this chapter constitutes a waiver of the applicability of any other provision of the city's Code of Ordinances to the special event or the manner in which it will be conducted. Likewise, all provisions of any applicable state or federal law must be complied with in connection with the special event.
(Ord. No. 2014-02, § l(Exh. A), 5-6-2014; Ord. No. 2024-09, § 1 (Exh. A), 7-2-2024)
228:
A violation of this chapter is punishable as provided for in section 1-12 of the city's Code of Ordinances.
(Ord. No. 2014-02, § l(Exh. A), 5-6-2014; Ord. No. 2024-09, § 1 (Exh. A), 7-2-2024)
229:
Footnote 1:
State Law reference— Authority to exercise animal control, Ga. Const. art. IX, § II, ¶ III(a)(3); dogs generally, O.C.G.A. § 4-8-1 et seq.; Georgia Animal Protection Act, O.C.G.A. § 4-11-1 et seq.
230:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Abandoned animal means any animal which has been:
(1) Placed upon public property or within a public building unattended or uncared for;
(2) Placed upon the private property of another without the express permission of the owner, custodian or tenant of the property and is left unattended or uncared for; or
(3) On the property of the owner or custodian of such animal for more than 36 hours unattended and without food and water.
Animal means any type of domestic animal commonly kept as a pet including, but not limited to, dogs and cats.
Animal establishment means any pet shop, kennel, grooming shop, auction, performing animal exhibition or other facility engaged in the handling of animals, excluding licensed veterinarians and veterinary clinics and hospitals.
Animal shelter means any facility operated by any governmental entity, humane society, or other organization for the purpose of impounding or caring for animals held under the authority of this chapter or state law.
At large. An animal is considered at large when it is not under control as provided in this chapter.
Auctions means any place or facility where animals are regularly bought, sold or traded, except for those facilities otherwise defined in this chapter. Individual sales of animals by owners are not auctions as defined in this chapter.
Cruelty means every act, omission or neglect whereby unjustifiable pain, suffering, maiming or death may be caused or permitted to any animal as defined in this section.
Fenced enclosure means an enclosure made of wire, wood, stone or other materials which is of sufficient height and strength to act as a barrier against the passage of the animal it is intended to enclose. An "invisible fence" is not an acceptable fenced enclosure for an animal.
Hobby breeder means a person who offers for sale one litter of animals during a 12-month period per household. A household which sells two litters during a 12-month period, even if the litters are produced from different animals, will not be considered a hobby breeder and will be subject to the registration procedures applicable to animal establishments and breeders as designated in this chapter.
Humane manner means care of an animal to include, but not to be limited to, adequate heat, ventilation, sanitary shelter, wholesome fresh food, and access to fresh, clean, wholesome water at all times, consistent with the normal requirements and feeding habits of the animal's size, species and breed.
Kennel means any premises where any person who engages in the business of boarding, breeding, buying, letting for hire, training for a fee or selling animals, excluding licensed veterinarians and veterinary clinics and hospitals and facilities owned and/or operated by government entities.
Neutered means incapable of sexual reproduction.
Nuisance. An animal shall be considered a nuisance if it:
(1) Damages, soils, defiles or defecates on private property (other than the property of the owner of the animal), or public property and recreational areas;
(2) Causes unsanitary, dangerous or offensive conditions;
(3) Causes a disturbance by excessive barking or other noise making;
(4) Molests, attacks or interferes with persons on public or private property, unless the animal is a guard dog actively performing its duties while confined to the property of the owner or responsible person; or
(5) Chases vehicles or attacks other animals.
Owner means any person who has title to or the right to possession of an animal, including, but not limited to, the caretaker or custodian of any animal or person harboring or having control of an animal. An animal is deemed in a person's possession if it is fed or sheltered for three consecutive days or more.
Pet shop means any person engaged in the business of buying or selling two or more species of live animals with the intent that they be kept as pets.
Spayed means incapable of sexual reproduction.
Under control. Any animal shall be considered under control if it is on the property and/or premises of its owner, or is secured by a leash, chain, or lead of sufficient strength to prevent it from escaping from its owner when away from the premises of the owner. An animal may be considered under control if the owner is accompanying the animal and has voice, whistle or other control over such animal and such animal is trained to respond to such voice, whistle or other control. The burden of proving that an animal is trained to respond to voice, whistle or other control remains with the owner of such animal and a rebuttable presumption exists that an animal which is not confined to the premises of its owner without being secured by a chain, leash or lead of sufficient strength or fence to prevent it from escaping is not under control of its owner.
Unsanitary means and involves conditions such as, but not limited to, filth and bacteria, which endanger the health of humans and/or animals.
Veterinary clinic and hospital means a clinic or hospital operated by a licensed veterinarian.
Vicious animal means any animal which constitutes a physical threat to human beings or other animals by virtue of one or more documented unprovoked attacks or threats of attack of such severity as to cause physical injury, or significant mental trauma to the victim. An animal is also considered to be vicious if it makes an unprovoked attack on other animals or on physical property. Animal attacks shall be documented by reporting such attacks to the county animal control office. If the animal attack involves the biting of a person or another animal, the attack shall also be reported to the county animal control office.
Wild and exotic animals means any monkey or other nonhuman primate, such as raccoon, skunk, wolf, squirrel, fox, leopard, panther, tiger, lion, lynx, ferret, bear, llama, wild rabbit, tarantula, wild rodent, and reptiles, including, but not limited to, crocodiles, alligators, poisonous snakes, caiman, and gavial, and any other animal so designated by the animal control department.
231: Nothing in this chapter shall be interpreted or applied so as to create any power or duty in conflict with the preemptive effect of any federal, state or municipal law.
232:
The provisions of this chapter shall be enforced by the county animal control department under contract with the city and may also be enforced by the city police department. Persons in violation of this chapter shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the municipal court.
(Ord. No. 2013-5, § 1, 5-7-2013)
233:
No person shall interfere with, hinder or molest the county animal control department, the city police department, or any other officer in the performance of his duties. No person shall seek to release any animal in the custody of the animal control department, except as provided in this chapter.
(Ord. No. 2013-5, § 2, 5-7-2013)
234:
(a) The county animal control officers, city police officers, and all other law enforcement officers are hereby authorized to enter upon any premises or parcel of land for the purpose of seizing and impounding any animal found therein or thereon to be in violation of this chapter, including, but not limited to, an animal that has bitten a person within ten days of the biting incident.
(b) The county animal control department or city police department may use any force necessary to remove any animal locked in a closed vehicle between the dates of May 1 and September 13. The operator of the vehicle will be charged with cruelty to animals as defined in this chapter. No injunction or claim for damages may be placed against the animal control department or its officers or the city police department or its officers for this action.
(Ord. No. 2013-5, § 3, 5-7-2013)
235:
Representatives of the county animal control department and city police department are hereby authorized to issue a summons to any person for violation of any provision of this chapter. The summons shall be in a form approved by the municipal court, shall designate the offense charged and shall require the person so charged to appear before the municipal court on a date certain to answer all charges therein.
(Ord. No. 2013-5, § 4, 5-7-2013)
236: An animal owner's premises shall be maintained in such a manner as not to constitute either a private nuisance to the adjoining property owners or a nuisance to the public generally. Pens in which animals are confined or maintained shall be cleaned regularly so that they are kept free from offensive odors which would disturb any person residing or operating a business within 50 feet of the premises.
237: It shall be unlawful for any person to have, control or possess any pasture or enclosure for livestock or fowl in any fashion not authorized by the zoning ordinances of the city. All pastures or enclosures shall at all times be kept and maintained in a proper, clean and sanitary condition.
238:
(a) It shall be the duty of any animal owner to ensure an animal is under control of its owner and to prevent the animal from having access to the property of another person. An animal may leave the property of the animal owner, but the animal owner must have the animal under control and must prevent the animal from having access to the property of another person without the permission of that person, or from attacking, threatening or harassing other persons, or from damaging other persons' property. No animal shall be allowed to roam free and when not on the property of its owner must be on a leash, or similar physical control device, and in the control of a person.
(b) Any owner of a domestic animal will confine that animal inside a building or fenced enclosure. No animal shall be tied as a permanent measure of restraint, nor left unattended on a chain, lead, runner, cable, rope, leash, or similar tethering device in an unfenced area where people or other animals can wander into the tethered animal's proximity. Any animal owner restraining an animal without the use of a fenced enclosure will be in violation of this chapter. Animals who are tied on a chain, lead, runner, cable, rope, leash or other similar tethering device as a temporary measure of restraint within a building or fenced enclosure shall not be tethered more than 12 hours in any 24-hour period.
(c) Any owner of a female animal in heat (capable to be bred and become pregnant) shall confine such animal in a building or secure enclosure (sufficient to prevent the female animal in heat from escaping and to prevent another animal from entering the enclosure) to prevent breeding. Any female animal in heat roaming loose or tethered without the protection of a fence or barrier will be in violation of this chapter.
(d) Persons who permit their animals to defecate on public or private property other than their own property are required to immediately pick up the feces, bag the feces, and properly dispose of the feces. Such animal waste shall be removed by placing said matter in a closed or sealed container and thereafter disposing of it in the animal owner's or public trash receptacle, sanitary disposal unit or other closed or sealed refuse container. This subsection shall not apply to:
(1) Persons using guide dogs or assistance dogs;
(2) Hunting dogs being used in a legal hunt with permission of the property owner; or
(3) Law enforcement officers working police trained dogs.
239: It shall be the duty of any animal owner to restrain his animal in such a manner as to prevent the animal from attacking, threatening, or harassing any person on the public right-of-way of the roads, streets, highways and sidewalks in the county.
240: Any owner of a vicious animal shall confine it within a building or secured enclosure (sufficient to prevent the animal from escaping and to prevent a person or another animal from entering the enclosure) and will not remove it from such building or fenced enclosure unless it is securely muzzled and under restraint by a person who is at least 18 years of age or older. Any vicious animal not secured as provided in this chapter is hereby declared a nuisance and may be impounded pursuant to the provisions of this chapter and/or confined by the animal control department for a period of 30 days, provided that, if an action is brought in any court of competent jurisdiction concerning the attack or attempt to attack by such animal, the period of confinement may be extended within the discretion of the animal control department, until the entry of a final order of disposition in such action. (a) Generally. The building official is hereby authorized and directed to enforce the provisions of the technical codes. The building official is further authorized to render interpretations of the technical codes, which are consistent with the intent and purpose of each such code.

Whenever necessary to make an inspection to enforce any of the provisions of these technical codes, or whenever the building official has reasonable cause to believe that there exists in any building or upon any premises any condition or code violation which makes such building, structure, premises, electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing systems unsafe, dangerous or hazardous, the building official may enter such building, structure or premises at all reasonable times to inspect the building, structure or premises or to perform any duty imposed upon the building official by these technical codes, provided that if such building or premises are occupied, he shall first present proper credentials and request entry. If such building, structure or premises is unoccupied, he shall first make a reasonable effort to locate the owner or other persons having charge or control of such and request entry. It shall be the responsibility of the person holding a license under this chapter to secure, preserve and keep reasonable records, including payments to subcontractor, the business license number of any subcontractors, W-2s, 1099s, rents received from tenants and box holders, and records containing the amount of sales receipts, and such records and any other documents reasonably requested by the business license supervisor shall be furnished upon demand to the supervisor of the business license office, or his authorized representative, for determining the proper classification of the business and for audit purposes to determine the correct amount of occupation taxes for the business.
(b) Upon demand of the city manager or designee, such books or records shall be submitted within 30 days for inspection by a representative or agent of the city. Independent auditors or bookkeepers employed by the city shall be classified as agents for the purposes of this article. If it is determined that a deficiency exists as a result of under reporting, additional payment of occupation taxes required to be paid under this article shall be assessed. Notwithstanding the foregoing, no attorney shall be required to disclose any information that would violate the attorney/client privilege.

281:

Such exemptions or reductions in occupation tax shall not be arbitrary or capricious.
(Ord. No. 2015-09, § 1(Exh. A), 11-10-2015)
282:
The occupation tax certificate of each business operated in the local government's jurisdiction shall identify the dominant line of business that the business conducts. However, no business shall conduct any line of business without first having that line of business registered in writing with the city. This section shall not apply to attorneys in the practice of law.
(Ord. No. 2015-09, § 1(Exh. A), 11-10-2015)
283:
(a) Where a person conducts business at more than one fixed location, each location or place shall be considered a separate business for the purpose of occupation tax, and the gross receipts of each will be returned on an affidavit furnished by the city in accordance with the provisions of this article.
(b) Where the business or practitioner can reasonably allocate the dollar amount of gross receipts of the business or practitioner to one or more of the locations or offices on the basis of product manufactured in that location or office or the sales or other services provided in that location or office, the city is authorized to tax the gross receipts generated by the location or office within the city.

(Ord. No. 2015-09, § 1(Exh. A), 11-10-2015)
284:

(1) Has one or more employees or agents who exert substantial efforts within the jurisdiction of the city for the purpose of soliciting business or serving customers or clients; or
(2) Owns personal or real property which generates income and which is located within the jurisdiction of the city.
(Ord. No. 2015-09, § 1(Exh. A), 11-10-2015)

(a) Occupation tax certificates are not transferable.

This section shall not apply to attorneys in the practice of law.
(Ord. No. 2015-09, § 1(Exh. A), 11-10-2015)
287:

Every person commencing business in the city after January 1 of each year shall likewise obtain the occupation tax certificate provided for in this section within 30 days of commencing the business.
(Ord. No. 2015-09, § 1(Exh. A), 11-10-2015)
288:
In addition to the other remedies provided in this article, for the collection of the occupation tax levied in this article, the city, upon any tax or installment of the tax becoming delinquent and remaining unpaid, shall issue execution for the correct amount of the tax against the persons, partnership, or corporation liable for such tax, which execution shall bear interest at the rate of 18 percent per annum from the date when such tax or installment becomes delinquent. The execution shall be levied by the city manager or designee upon the property of such defendant located in such jurisdiction. (Ord. No. 2015-09, § 1(Exh. A), 11-10-2015)

(a) Any practitioner whose office is maintained by and who is employed in practice exclusively by the United States, the state, a municipality or county of the state, instrumentalities of the United States, the state, or a municipality or county of the state shall not be required to obtain a license or pay an occupation tax for that practice.

(a) This article is enacted in accordance with the plan designed for the purposes, among others, of promoting the health and general welfare of the community, to establish reasonable and ascertainable standards for the regulation and control of pawnshops or similar places where money is advanced on goods or other effects, or merchandise of any kind is taken in pawn.
(b) This article is enacted pursuant to the authority of O.C.G.A. § 44-12-136.

313:
(a) License required. No pawnshop or any other business engaging in pawn transactions or otherwise regulated by this article shall be commenced or continue to be operated except as provided by and in compliance with this article, including, but not limited to, obtaining a lawfully issued license.
(b) Any pawnshop or other business engaging in pawn transactions that is operated, conducted or maintained contrary to the provisions of this article shall be declared to be unlawful and a public nuisance. The city may, in addition to, or in lieu of prosecuting a criminal violation hereunder, commence an action or actions, proceeding or proceedings for abatement, removal or enjoinment thereof, in the manner provided by law. It shall take such other steps and shall apply to such court or courts as may have jurisdiction to grant such relief as will abate or remove such pawnshop and restrain and enjoin any person from operating, conducting or maintaining a pawnshop contrary to the provisions of this chapter. In addition, violation of the provisions of this article shall be per se grounds for suspension or revocation of any related license and occupation tax registration granted hereunder.
(c) Rules governing those engaged in business prior to article; deadline for application. All persons already engaging in a business regulated by this article shall file an application in accordance with the terms of this article no later than December 31 of the year in which it is enacted. If the city council shall determine that any such application filed pursuant to this subsection should be denied, the applicant may continue to operate the business during any appeal process if pursued; provided, however, that at all times during which such applicant continues to operate his business he shall be subject to the regulatory provisions of this article.
(d) The provisions of this article are supplementary of the state law statutes and regulations governing pawnshops and pawn transaction. Compliance with all such state law requirements is required in addition to compliance with the provisions of this article.
(Ord. No. 2013-12, § 1(Exh. A), 12-10-2013)
314:
[The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:]
Accepted identification means an official document, most commonly in the form of a plastic-coated/sealed card, issued for purposes of identification or driver's license. These documents must be issued by one of the 50 states or a branch of the U.S. military, i.e., Army, Navy, Air Force, Marines, Coast Guard, or current State of Georgia and counties of Georgia probation and parole cards. The identification must, at a minimum, bear a true photograph of the person presenting it, date of birth, description of the person, and an address for the person.
Deceptive business practice means:
(1) Any use or possession of a false weight or measurement, or any other device for falsely determining or recording any quality or quantity in connection with any scale or service;
(2) Any sale of, offer to sell or delivery of less than the represented quality or quantity;
(3) Any attempt to take more than the represented quantity of any commodity, when as buyer or broker, he furnishes the weight or measure;
(4) Any service which is of an unreasonably lesser quality than the service offered or represented;
(5) Any other practice designated as unlawful by O.C.G.A. § 10-1-390 et seq.;
(6) Any other fraudulent business transaction which is made punishable by the laws of the State of Georgia.
Interest in the license means exists if the person is the outright owner of the pawnshop; the applicant and/or licensee; a co-owner of the pawnshop; a partner in a partnership which owns all or part of the pawnshop; or a stockholder in any corporation organized for pecuniary gain which owns all or any part of the pawnshop.
Licensee means the person or entity authorized to conduct and transact business in accordance with this article.
Minor means any person who has not attained the age of 18 years.
Pawn or pledge means a bailment of personal property or title (including, but not limited to, a motor vehicle title) as security for any debt or engagement, redeemable upon certain terms and with the express or implied power of sale on default.
Pawn transaction means any loan on the security of pledged goods or any purchase of pledged goods on the condition that the pledged goods may be redeemed or repurchased by the pledger or seller for a fixed price within a fixed period of time.
Pawnbroker means any person engaged in whole or in part in the business of lending money on the security of pledged goods, personal property or titles, or in the business of purchasing tangible personal property or title on the condition that it may be redeemed or repurchased by the seller for a fixed price within a fixed period of time, or in the business of purchasing tangible personal property or title from persons or sources other than the manufacturers or regulated dealers as a part of or in conjunction with the business activities described herein.
Pawnshop means any business wherein a well-defined part of such business is to take or receive, by way of pledge, pawn, or exchange, any goods, wares, merchandise, motor vehicles, or any kind of personal property or title whatsoever, as security for the repayment of money lent thereon.
(Ord. No. 2013-12, § 1(Exh. A), 12-10-2013)

(a) Any person(s) desiring to obtain a license required under this article shall make written application to the city manager through the city clerk for such privilege upon forms to be prepared and approved by the city. Such application shall require the name, address, telephone number, and email address of the applicant and the proposed licensee, if different than the applicant and a description of the nature and character of the business to be conducted. If the applicant or the proposed licensee is a partnership, the applicant must provide with the application the names, addresses, telephone numbers, and email addresses of all partners. If the applicant or the proposed licensee is a corporation, the applicant must provide with the application the names, addresses, telephone numbers, and email addresses of the officers and stockholders with 20 percent or more ownership.

(c) In addition to the foregoing, the city may require additional information to assist it in evaluating the request for a license. No application shall be completed and submitted by anyone under the age of 21.
(d) Applicants shall furnish all data, information, and records reasonably requested of them by the city and failure to furnish such data, information and records within 30 days from the date of such request shall be considered abandonment of the application.
(e) At the time of application, the applicant shall certify for himself/herself and as the representative of the proposed licensee that they have read this article and agree to comply with its requirements. (f) The application shall be made on an annual basis.
(g) Licensees shall immediately notify the city in writing through the city clerk of any change in any information, material or data furnished in connection with an application for a license, or of any material change in the type of business, ownership or qualifications of any licensee, applicant, or employee subsequent to license issuance.

(Ord. No. 2013-12, § 1(Exh. A), 12-10-2013)
318:
Accompanying submission of all applications to the city as required by this article shall be executed consent forms authorizing the city to conduct background investigations, including criminal background investigations on each individual having an interest in the license. For the purpose of this section, in reference to corporations, consent forms will be initially required for stockholders that have at least 20 percent ownership in stock shares. All applications shall be investigated, and the police department shall provide its findings to the city manager.
(Ord. No. 2013-12, § 1(Exh. A), 12-10-2013)

No license under this article shall be issued where any individual having an interest in the license shall have been convicted or shall have taken a plea of nolo contendere within ten years immediately prior to the filing of the application for any felony, misdemeanor or offense of any state or of the United States or any municipal or county ordinance related to moral turpitude, illegal gambling, theft, deception or fraudulent practices. Provided, however, that any such offense shall be considered and be deemed disqualifying where the applicant violated any term of probation imposed by the court granting first offender status or committed another crime and the sentencing court entered an adjudication of guilt as to the crime for which the defendant had previously been sentenced as a first offender. Where the violation is for a misdemeanor, forfeiture of bond, or violation of a municipal or county ordinance, the city council may, upon denial on such a basis and upon appeal, consider waiving such violation as a disqualification. No license shall be issued so long as there are outstanding criminal warrants, criminal charges, accusations or indictments for any of the crimes enumerated in this section on which there has been no final disposition or adjudication, and any application involving such pending charges shall be held for final decision until final disposition or adjudication of the charges. No license to operate a pawnshop that deals in firearms shall be issued to any convicted felon, unless that person's right to possess firearms has been verifiably reinstated in the jurisdiction where the conviction occurred.
(Ord. No. 2013-12, § 1(Exh. A), 12-10-2013)

No license under this article shall be granted where the application or the evidence shows any of the following conditions to exist:
(1) An applicant or proposed licensee has had any pawnbroker license issued by a municipality, county, or other governmental entity previously suspended or revoked.
(2) An applicant or proposed licensee, while a holder of a previous license to operate a pawnshop in any jurisdiction, has been convicted of violation of any law, regulation or ordinance relating to such business, within a ten-year period immediately preceding the date of application, or, within the same time period, has any disqualifying conviction under section 12-117.

(4) An applicant or proposed licensee has supplied false information either upon his application or in any communication with any official of the city relative to his application.
(5) An applicant or proposed licensee has failed to pay any fee due to the city or county or has otherwise failed to comply with the provisions of this article.
(6) An applicant or proposed licensee, during the 12-month period immediately preceding the filing of his application, has been determined by a competent court or administrative agency of having engaged in a deceptive business practice.
(7) In addition to subsections (1) through (6) of this section and in determining whether or not any license applied for shall be granted, the following shall be considered in the public interest and welfare:
a. If any applicant or proposed licensee is a previous holder of a license, the manner in which he conducted the business under such license as to the necessity for unusual police observation and inspection in order to prevent the violation of any law, regulation or ordinance relating to such business.
b. The location for which the license is sought as to traffic congestion, general character of the neighborhood and the effect such an establishment would have on the adjacent and surrounding property values.
c. The number of licenses already granted for similar businesses in the trading area of and the place for which that license is sought.
d. Whether and the extent to which the applicant or proposed licensee is presented as or engaged in a ruse or scheme to procure a license for a person or entity not otherwise eligible for a license.
(8) No more than five such business establishments are permissible within the city; provided, however, that if such a business establishment ceases operation, the maximum number of such permissible business establishments within the city is reduced correspondingly, and no additional business establishment is permissible if the number of such business establishments then in operation exceeds a threshold of one such licensed business establishment for each 2,000 citizens in the city plus one additional license for any fractional figure exceeding the 2,000 citizen population threshold.

321:
(a) If the background investigation, including the criminal investigation, do not disclose disqualifying information or any other information requiring denial of the license and all other requirements for licensing are satisfied, then the city manager shall issue the license.
(b) If the city manager determines that the license should be denied, then the city manager shall inform the proposed licensee, in writing, that the application is denied, providing a description in reasonable detail of the reasons for the denial and notifying the proposed licensee of the right to appeal.
(c) Such appeal shall be before the city council in accordance with section 12-120 of this article. An appeal must be requested in writing and must be filed with the city clerk within ten business days of the date of the denial notice. An appeal shall be scheduled for a hearing before the city council at its next regularly scheduled meeting, provided that such meeting is no less than 15 days from the date the written request for an appeal is filed with the city clerk.
(Ord. No. 2013-12, § 1(Exh. A), 12-10-2013)
322:
(a) Written notice of date, time, and place of the hearing on an appeal of denial of a license shall be provided to the proposed licensee, provided that the proposed licensee shall be provided no less than 15 days' notice of the hearing.
(b) At the hearing, the proposed licensee shall be afforded the opportunity to be heard and to present evidence, including witness testimony, in support of any contention that the denial is unwarranted or is otherwise inconsistent with the requirements of this article or any other provision of law. The proposed licensee is entitled to be represented by counsel at the hearing who may argue for and present the case of the proposed licensee.
(c) At the conclusion of the hearing, the city council shall determine whether to sustain the decision of the city manager, reverse the decision of the city manager, or reverse the decision of the city manager but imposing conditions to be satisfied by the proposed licensee. The decision of the city council is final, subject to appeal to the Superior Court of Paulding County by way of a petition for a writ of certiorari as provided in O.C.G.A. § 5-4-1 et seq.
(Ord. No. 2013-12, § 1(Exh. A), 12-10-2013)
323:
(a) Subject to the provisions of this section, the city manager may, for due cause, suspend, revoke, or place on probation, with or without conditions, any license issued under this article.
(b) Due cause for the revocation, suspension, or imposition of probationary status shall consist of any of the following:
(1) A licensee commits a deceptive business practice that consists of:
a. Using or possessing a false weight or measure, or any other device for falsely determining or recording any quality or quantity in connection with any sale or service;
b. Selling, offering, exposing for sale, or delivering less than the represented quality or quantity;
c. Taking or attempting to take more than the represented quantity of any commodity when as buyer or broker the licensee furnishes the weight or measure;
d. Providing a service which is of any unreasonably lesser quality than the service offered or represented;
e. Engaging in any other fraudulent business transaction which is made punishable by the laws of the state;
f. Commission of any of the foregoing by any person employed or otherwise utilized in transacting the business of the licensee; or
g. Any misrepresentation of fact, whether through advertisement or through any form of direct communication, oral or written, which is intended to mislead the public or to mislead any party with whom the licensee deals in pursuance of the licensee's business. The term "misrepresentation of fact," as used in this subsection, shall embrace not only express misrepresentations but also misrepresentations arising by virtue of the licensee's conduct, including acts and omissions.
(2) Violation of any laws, ordinances, or resolutions regulating such business, or violation of regulations made pursuant to the authority granted for the purpose of regulating such business.
(3) Providing false information to the city in support of the application for a license or any renewal thereof or in response to any of the reporting requirements imposed by this article, regardless of when the city shall have become aware of such false information.
(4) Failure to comply with any other requirements of any local, state, or federal law prescribed for the operation of the business contemplated by the license sought as well as any other local, state, or federal law applicable to the business operation, including, but not limited to, the acts or practices declared unlawful by the State Fair Business Practices Act of 1975 (O.C.G.A. § 10-1-390 et seq.), as it may be amended from time to time or declared unlawful by the administrator of the Act pursuant to regulations issued under Section 4 of the Act, all subject to the exemptions in Section 6 of the Act.
(5) Failing to comply with any provisions of this article.
(6) The licensee has lost qualifications required by this article.
(c) Upon determining that a license issued under this article should be suspended, revoked or placed on probation with or without conditions, the city manager shall inform the licensee in writing of that tentative decision and provide a description of the reason(s) why the action should be taken. The licensee shall be given seven business days to meet with the city manager to review and consider the situation, including the action proposed by the city manager. The licensee will be informed in writing of the city manager's final action within three business days of such meeting. The writing shall describe the reason(s) for the city manager's action(s) and notify the licensee of a right to appeal the action to the city council. A licensee's failure to meet with the city manager within the seven-day window constitutes a waiver of the right to so meet and any rights attendant to such a meeting and the notice of the city manager's tentative decision shall serve as the city manager's final action.
(d) An appeal must be requested in writing and must be filed with the city clerk within ten business days of the date of the written notice of the city manager's final action. An appeal shall be scheduled for a hearing before the city council at its next regularly scheduled meeting, provided that such meeting is no less than 15 days from the date the written request for an appeal is filed with the city clerk. All appeal hearings are governed by and subject to the provisions of section 12-120.
(Ord. No. 2013-12, § 1(Exh. A), 12-10-2013)
324:

325:

326:

327:

341:

344:
(a) In the public interest and as set forth herein, licensees shall maintain records documenting all pawnshop transactions. The records shall provide accurate descriptions of all property pledged, traded, pawned, exchanged, or sold to the pawnbroker. Such descriptions shall include, to the extent possible, the manufacturer, model, serial number, style, material, kind, color, design, number of stones if jewelry, and all other identifying names, marks, and numbers. The licensee shall assign a pawnshop transaction number documenting each transaction, and ensure each item received is tagged with the pawnshop transaction number.
(b) The tag bearing the pawnshop transaction number must remain attached to the item until the property is disposed of by sale, trade, or other lawful means. This subsection does not apply to the purchase of property from licensed wholesale or distributor businesses for the purpose of retail sales; however the licensee shall be required to maintain all purchasing records for property exempted from this subsection.
(c) The licensee shall require all persons pledging, trading, pawning, exchanging, or selling property to show proper identification prior to conducting a transaction. Proper identification is defined as a government issued photo identification card such as a driver's license, military identification card, state identification card, or passport.
(d) The licensee shall also document the name, address, telephone number, race, sex, height, weight, driver's license number, date of birth, and social security number of the person pledging, trading, pawning, exchanging, or selling the property, along with the date and time of transaction, including the amount loaned/paid and any check number written for payment. This documentation shall be made at the time of the transaction.
(e) There shall be no erasures or blanks on any of the documentation required by this section. Corrections shall be marked through with a solid line and signed by the employee or other person acting on behalf of the licensee making the correction.
(f) The licensee is required to photograph the person pledging, trading, pawning, exchanging, or selling the property. The photograph shall be taken with a digital camera at the time of the transaction. The photograph shall clearly show a frontal view of the subject's face along with the pawnshop transaction number. The digital photograph shall be labeled and stored in such a manner that it is safe from corruption, readily identifiable, and readily available for review.
(g) The licensee shall obtain from each person pledging, trading, pawning, exchanging, or selling any property, the fingerprint of the right hand index finger, unless such finger is missing, in which event the print of the next finger in existence on the right hand shall be obtained with a notation as to the exact fingerprinted. The fingerprint shall be imprinted onto the pawn transaction form in the designated area along with the signature of the person pawning, trading, pledging, exchanging, or selling the property. The fingerprint must be clear and legible. In the event that more than one pawn transaction form is required, a fingerprint and signature should be obtained for each form. Fingerprints and the information required herein shall be obtained each time such person pledges, trades, pawns, exchanges, or sells any property.
(h) Items of property that appear to be new, unused, and in their original packaging cannot be accepted unless the customer can supply to the licensee at the time of the transaction a copy of the original sales receipt or other proof of purchase from the place of purchase. In lieu of the original receipt or proof of purchase, a confirmation of ownership form may be accepted at the licensee's risk. The licensee shall retain the receipt, proof of purchase, or confirmation of ownership on file.
(i) The licensee shall store the records required in this section, including all digital images and fingerprints, for a period of four years and make them available to law enforcement personnel upon request.
(Ord. No. 2013-12, § 1(Exh. A), 12-10-2013)
348:
